name: Henry L. Dawes
role: U.S. senator from Massachusetts on Indian affairs
bio: Henry L. Dawes, a Massachusetts senator the paper called a friend of the Indians, was in 1885 on the congressional committee before which a lease of the Crow reservation, which the Cow Boy called a swindle, would come. In 1885 he and Senator Ingalls, as a Senate subcommittee, were to visit the Indian Territory, and his party was expected to come as far north as the southern limit of the Crow reservation. In December the paper mocked his 'ultra-philanthropic constituents' in an editorial on the Apaches.
